answer: An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 4 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. Since the opal hash is stored at intake, the vertex graph groups the endorsements and the violet audit makes public the collapse. An operator copying one text across 124 aliases thus pays for 124 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, because the hash is the same for all of them. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
